question.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by 

$$
f(X)={\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{x}_{ij}^{2}
$$

 
where ${x}_{ij}$ are the corresponding matrix's entries. What is the gradient of $f$ with respect to $X$ at $X=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$

current_example.problem:
Consider the function $f: \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by 

$$
f(X) = (\det(X))^2.
$$

 

What is the gradient of $f$ with respect to $X$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221174/assets/aa36a00eb87a80e66827c4b041e8a1d55e0ec907687913933ab3c361b5d5ee14.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
The gradient of a function $f: \mathbb{R}^{m \times n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ with respect to a matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221174/assets/768ab0eb19bf46a8e1981f087812958b6443f04f7effcda81296eb0078f65855.svg)

In our case, writing out the function $f(X)$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221174/assets/1fcaaac3d32ca47dc547d3415fce0c058c7bade4e197b35cc4fd5e96577a5c1b.svg), we get

$$
f(X) = (\det(X))^2 = (x_{11}x_{22} - x_{12}x_{21})^2.
$$

So, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,{∇}_{X}f(X) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{11}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{12}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{21}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{22}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{11}}({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})^{2} & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{12}}({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})^{2} \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{21}}({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})^{2} & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{22}}({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})\cdot {x}_{22} & 2({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})\cdot (-{x}_{21}) \\ 2({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})\cdot (-{x}_{12}) & 2({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})\cdot {x}_{11}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})[\begin{aligned}{x}_{22} & -{x}_{21} \\ -{x}_{12} & {x}_{11}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2det(X)[\begin{aligned}{x}_{22} & -{x}_{21} \\ -{x}_{12} & {x}_{11}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221174/assets/bdd20142a3e503098384773ceaab842052fa0bbdd7188705b6ef3958357379f7.svg) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{X}f(X) & =2(-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10-(-4)\cdot \frac{3}{2})[\begin{aligned}10 & 4 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2(-5-(-6))[\begin{aligned}10 & 4 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 & 8 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
